She reports that the stiffness lasts for more than an hour each day and improves with activity.
She has noted swelling in her wrists and proximal interphalangeal joints.
She denies family history of autoimmune diseases.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago, 10 pack-year history.

encounters.cc: Bilateral wrist pain and morning stiffness with numbness and tingling in fingers

lines: Bilateral wrist pain and morning stiffness with numbness and tingling in fingers
The patient is a 52-year-old female with a history of hypothyroidism and rheumatoid arthritis who returns for follow-up.
She presents with a 6-month history of bilateral wrist pain and morning stiffness lasting more than one hour.
She reports that her symptoms improve with activity.
She also complains of numbness and tingling in her thumb, index, and middle fingers, which worsens at night.
Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
She takes for which she takes levothyroxine.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
On physical examination, there is tenderness and swelling over the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints.
Wrist flexion for 60 seconds elicits tingling in the median nerve distribution.
X-rays of the hands show periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions.

lines: Severe vulvar itching persistent for six months

encounters.cc: Persistent vulvar itching worse at night unresponsive to hydrocortisone

lines: Persistent vulvar itching worse at night unresponsive to hydrocortisone
This 53-year-old female with rheumatoid arthritis and hypothyroidism returns to the Obstetrics & Gynecology clinic for ongoing vulvar symptoms previously evaluated in September and November 2020.
She presents with a 6-month history of persistent vulvar itching and discomfort.
She reports that the symptoms are worse at night and have not improved with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream.
She denies any vaginal discharge or bleeding.
Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism.
She takes for which she takes levothyroxine.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
On physical examination, you note several white, patchy plaques on the vulva with areas of scarring and loss of the normal architecture, including the labia minora.
There is no palpable inguinal lymphadenopathy.
A vulvar punch biopsy is performed, and histopathology reveals hyperkeratosis, atrophic epidermis, and a band-like infiltrate of lymphocytes in the dermis.

lines: Night sweats, fevers, unexplained weight loss, and enlarging neck mass

The patient is a 55-year-old female with hypothyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate, and prior colorectal neoplasia, who presents with a 2-month history of night sweats, unexplained weight loss of 10 pounds, and low-grade fevers.
She mentions feeling a 'lump' on the side of her neck, which has gradually increased in size.
She has been on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone for the past 8 years.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 10 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
On physical examination, you note a non-tender, firm, and rubbery lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter in the left cervical chain.
An excisional biopsy of the lymph node is performed.
